subject: Private VPC connectivity: egress-IP plan & PrivateLink feasibility (post-demo follow-up)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir@datafin.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Private VPC connectivity: follow-up from today's demo

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for joining the demo earlier. Quick recap and the network info we'll need to scope a Private VPC deployment versus Dedicated/Hosted options: 

- Deployment preference: you mentioned strong preference for an inbound control plane (no public endpoints) — looks like PrivateLink or VPC peering will be the likely options.
- Network asks we need from DataFin's side:
  - Which connectivity model is required by your security team: AWS PrivateLink, VPC peering, or direct on-prem VPN?
  - Current firewall allowlist process — do you accept a static set of egress IPs from Redwood, or do you require NAT behind your side?
  - Any mandatories in firewall rules (ports, protocols, mTLS)?
  - Point of contact for your network/security (we can work with them directly)

Attached is a short Private VPC quickstart that outlines what we need on day 0. If you can share the answers above + any existing firewall policy (or the person who owns it), we will draft a connectivity plan and a mutual action plan.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) DataFin confirms connectivity model + network contact (by EOD Thu)
2) Redwood provides egress IP candidates and a two-option connectivity plan (PrivateLink vs peering)
3) Schedule a 30-min network deep-dive with your netops + our infra eng (Karthik/Laura)

Thanks — I'll loop in Karthik and Vanessa for the technical scoping and timeline.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 10:37:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Private VPC connectivity: follow-up from today's demo

Neha — thanks for the thorough recap. Quick answers from our side: 

- Preferred model: AWS PrivateLink (our security team does not want ingress from public IPs into our VPC).
- Egress policy: we typically allow outbound to specific vendor IP ranges via our perimeter firewall. We can accept a small static allowlist of egress IPs, but need a written list at least 72 hours before cutover for change control.
- TLS/mutual auth: we require TLS1.2+, and will prefer mutual TLS for service-to-service control plane connections.

Looping in Aisha (netops lead) as requested — she will coordinate firewall/allowlist details. Aisha: can we set up a 30-min slot for this week?

Attached our current network constraints doc for visibility.

—Samir
Samir Rao
Head of Product | DataFin Analytics
samir@datafin.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: DataFin PrivateLink approach + action items

Hi team —

Thanks Neha. Based on Samir's note, PrivateLink is the preferred route. A few technical clarifications I want to capture before the netops call: 

- PrivateLink control plane: Redwood can publish an NLB-backed interface endpoint per-customer. That supports inbound from your VPC into a face-to-face endpoint.
- Egress IPs: Redwood cannot guarantee arbitrary per-customer egress IPs from our shared Hosted fleet. For Private VPC we offer two approaches:
  1) Redwood-provided static egress IPs from our Dedicated egress pool (requires a minimal Dedicated reserve or dedicated NAT egress)
  2) Customer-managed egress: DataFin routes outbound through your NAT/GW and we avoid flexible IP changes on our side.
- mTLS: we support mTLS for control-plane connections; implementation requires cert exchange and we'll share an ops-level endpoint.

Action items: 
- Laura: can you prepare a candidate egress-IP list (CIDR / single-IP choices) we can propose to DataFin? Include both Dedicated egress pool suggestions and notes on potential port ranges.
- Neha/Vanessa: schedule 30-min network deep-dive with Samir/Aisha + Laura.
- I'll draft the mutual-action-plan and include the timeline for cert exchange and allowlist dates.

I've attached a working mutual-action-plan template — I'll populate after netops call.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachment: mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Subject: Private VPC connectivity: proposed plan & next steps (PrivateLink option)

Samir / Aisha —

Thanks for confirming PrivateLink as your preferred model. Based on our internal scoping call, here are two feasible options and the recommended next steps: 

Option A — PrivateLink with Redwood-provided egress IPs (recommended)- What it is: Redwood publishes an Interface Endpoint (NLB-backed). We assign static egress IPs from our Dedicated egress pool that you can allowlist.
- Pros: minimal routing changes on your side, static allowlist we provide, faster cutover (~2 weeks after cert/allowlist approval).
- Cons: requires a small Dedicated egress commitment (covers the static egress allocation).

Option B — PrivateLink with customer-managed egress- What it is: DataFin hosts NAT/GW and controls outbound IPs.
- Pros: no Redwood Dedicated commitment; you control egress IPs and rotation process.
- Cons: requires you to provide a static egress IP and route outbound traffic accordingly; slightly more operational work on your side.

Immediate asks for DataFin: 
1) Confirm preferred option (A or B) by EOD Thu 11/12.
2) If Option A: confirm acceptance of candidate egress IPs (attached). We need final allowlist 72 hours before cutover.
3) If Option B: provide the egress IP(s) and NAT details.
4) Provide two 30-min windows for a network deep-dive this week so Laura can walk through the endpoint and certificate exchange process.

Next steps from Redwood after we hear back: fill in MAP with dates (mutual-action-plan.xlsx), provide cert exchange instructions, and prepare the interface endpoint description for your security review.

Thanks — looping Aisha for scheduling. Happy to jump on a call if you prefer to go over options.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
